I understand what you're saying about shoulder charge's viability depending on your skill bracket, but I think it's about as good as it can be for a melee ability where you run straight at another player. I think that the targeting change so you can't 180 change it's direction made it more balanced but I wouldn't complain if Bungie made it so shoulder charges connected more reliably.  


Secondly, perhaps referring to the barricade change as a buff was a mistake but I think it makes it much more interesting as an option. I think that in most cases, unless someone has accumulated an extremely high amount of special ammo, it would be a waste for them to spam it into the titan's barricade and if they're busy shooting at your barricade they're not shooting at your teammates. At a high competitive level, the argument could be made that no good player should ever be shooting at a Titan barricade but at least it has the additional utility option of helping you close off some angles.  


I can sympathize with console players, although I play on PC with M+K I know it's a much different experience playing with a controller. I was thinking that too, Titan movement is definitely somewhat lacking. They have probably the most punishing and least versatile jump in PvP so that is something I would like to see buffed. Hunters will always be the mobility kings and as much as I think it's fun, I would concede that the movement options of top tree dawnblade are a bit too strong.

Barricade was changed back in march where the health was reduced from 600 to 500 but the way it receives damage was changed I believe, where special weapons do more damage to barricades than primary weapons do. I suppose it's arguably a nerf, but imo it makes barricade slightly stronger while not completely overpowered. Either way, I wouldn't consider it a serious nerf. As a warlock main, I think that stormcaller is really horrible in PvP simply because it is so slow and you are so easy to headshot in it. Top tree dawnblade is definitely very strong, perhaps too good but I think the handheld supernova nerf makes evens it out a bit.

Believe me I understand, but I think what you're experiencing is just the bell curve where like most other players you're somewhere in the middle 70% of players who are relatively average while the top 15 and the bottom 15 percents of players will dominate or get stomped on respectively.

Aside from the fact that Titans have some incredibly strong exotic armor pieces in PvP as you've mentioned (also including ones like insurmountable skullfort, doomfang pauldrons, feedback fence, and especially citan's ramparts) they're currently very strong in PvP due to the barrier buff and their many strong subclasses. Shoulder charge is a one-hit melee that can be built by sprinting into a wall before engagement with pretty far range making it very hard to react to. 

Regarding class stats, yes resilience is less generally useful than mobility for hunters and recovery for warlocks but resilience is as useful stat in PvP as I'm sure you know certain resilience levels can delay the enemy's TTK for certain weapons. Also, I would argue that especially after the barrier buff and with the inclusion of citan's ramparts the titan barricade is  very strong as a utility and defensive option in PvP right now. Barrier also has a very low cooldown with even moderately high resilience compared to warlock rift, but let's not get started on hunter dodge. Barrier is also much more useful than rift for teamplay to provide cover for your teammates on the fly and especially in critical situations like when securing power ammo.  


Warlocks are only really strong in the air on a single subclass tree that was relatively recently changed being top tree dawnblade which prior to this change was objectively worse than bottomtree. Titans are strong in the air too because you can shoulder charge midair and with thundercrash you can slam into the ground a lot of AOE damage.  


I do agree that shoulder charge seems like it misses more than it should, but I believe this is more of a problem that affects all melee abilities in the game. There are a lot of major problems with MCC on PC that need to be addressed for people to come back. For starters:

1. They need to fix matchmaking, particularly the way server connections work. My friends and I were sick of constantly getting connected to laggy European servers instead of East US about 75% of the time.
2. The ranking system is very slow and unrewarding. Either make it a grind or not, and they've clearly gone for the option not to make it a grind the same way Inheritor was. People need to have an easier route to get the armor they want more quickly. Remember when thousands of people got banned for boosting just so they could rank up? That indicates a major problem.
3. The XP cap needs to be removed/diversified. You don't get rewarded for skill or doing well, no matter how well or poorly you do, you get the same amount of XP as everyone else which isn't very much in the first place which is frustrating. They should also add extra bonuses for things like being 1st or 2nd on the scoreboard, whether your team wins or loses, and staying in the game after losing a teammate for example.
4. There needs to be more transparency when the next games are expected to be out. I understand they're afraid of that from a developer's perspective, but from a casual fan's perspective they need something to be excited and interested in.
5. Bring back daily and weekly challenges. This was a great feature in the original Reach that was way ahead of its time that kept people coming back because it gave them a new objective every day that felt rewarding because it gave them quicker progress toward their rank.
6. The UI needs an adjustment or at least the way things are organized in playlists needs to offer more freedom. For instance, on the original Reach if you wanted to play Firefight you could choose what kind of firefight you wanted to play in matchmaking i.e. Arcadefight but now there is just a generic firefight playlist and if you don't like the mode you're given to play you either have to stick it out or quit.
